purpose: Select nested hierarchy nodes with expansion, mixed ancestor state, optional local search, and keyboard tree navigation while leaving resource meaning to the consumer.
useWhen: delegated resource scope needs nested selection
tenant, Farm, location, or cage structures need visible ancestor context
avoidWhen: the component would need to decide permission or authorization meaning
accessibility: Uses tree and treeitem semantics with aria-level, aria-posinset, aria-setsize, aria-expanded, aria-selected, and linked helper text.
Roving focus supports Arrow, Home, End, Space, and Enter without adding a second keyboard model.
Partial selection has a visible mixed marker and an explicit screen-reader announcement.
responsive: Keeps the tree inside a bounded scroll owner so long hierarchies do not expand the page indefinitely.
Rows wrap long labels and retain shared touch-target geometry on narrow Web layouts.
motion: Uses shared transition variables for focus, selection, and expansion affordances.
Respects prefers-reduced-motion through the global motion contract.

keyboard: Space and Enter select without changing expansion meaning
touch: branch expansion and selection retain separate touch targets
nested rows remain readable on compact surfaces
validation: consumer owns authorization and scope meaning
compatibility: Consumes the existing @ten4seven/ui export and catalog entry.
A consumer may continue using the existing Web props and event callbacks.
No product profile or route-specific primitive is introduced.
inputContract.intent: Commit a bounded selection value or set of values.

dataCollection.intent: Select one or more nodes in a hierarchy with mixed descendant state.
useWhen: a form or scope picker needs parent/descendant selection semantics
avoidWhen: navigation has one active node; use TreeView
dataCollection.rowCountSuitability: bounded selectable hierarchy with consumer-owned child loading
consumerOwns: scope meaning, selected IDs, permissions, and persistence
ten4sevenOwns: mixed selection, tree semantics, keyboard movement, and filter presentation
compatibility: TreeSelect remains a rejected duplicate of the hierarchy/input contracts.
